cards.front: The File class is misleadingly named. What does it actually represent?
cards.back: A pathname — a file or a directory — not an open file
cards.extra: It answers questions about the filesystem: does it exist, is it a directory, list its contents. Reading and writing happen through streams.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::02 File Operations

cards.back: A String[] of names, not File objects
cards.extra: An array because the set is fixed at the moment you ask. Use listFiles() for File objects, and a FilenameFilter to restrict the listing.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::02 File Operations

cards.front: What is the difference between an InputStream and a Reader?
cards.extra: Readers decode bytes using a charset, which is what you want for text. Using a byte stream for text is the classic encoding bug.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.back: Wraps another stream and adds behaviour — buffering, compression, counting — without changing the interface
cards.extra: This is the Decorator pattern: you compose streams by nesting them. That design is why Java has many small I/O classes instead of one giant one.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: Why does Java's I/O library use so many small classes?
cards.back: Because streams are composed: source + buffering + formatting, combined by wrapping
cards.extra: Each class does one thing and delegates to the one inside it. The alternative — a class per combination — would explode combinatorially.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: What does RandomAccessFile allow that other streams do not?
cards.back: Reading and writing at an arbitrary position via seek()
cards.extra: Normal streams are sequential. RandomAccessFile treats the file as an array of bytes, which suits fixed-size record files.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::02 File Operations
